rubric.criterion: Truth Index computation — canonical scoring engine
rubric.a_plus: Single authoritative computeTruthIndex() function using weighted TrustComponent model (title_document=30, landlord_identity=25, agent_physical_visit=20, price_market_check=10, no_active_disputes=10, legal_consent=5). Score = Σ(passed ? weight : 0) / Σ(weights) × 100, clamped 0–100, persisted to listing.truthIndex via syncTruthIndex(). All scoring deterministic, no Math.random(), no placeholder stubs.
rubric.current_state: Two competing implementations exist. lodgist/lib/trust/computeTruthIndex.ts is the canonical component-based engine wired to the trust API route. lodgist/lib/actions/calculateTruthIndex.ts is an older property-based implementation (5 categories: images/description/landlord/price/reviews) that persists to TruthIndexScore per user, not per listing. Both are active code paths. The fraudChecks.js package has additional fraud signal scoring (duplicate phone=40, price anomaly=15–30, stock photo=25, reverse image search=10–60) but is not wired into the canonical truth index flow.
rubric.evidence: lodgist/lib/trust/computeTruthIndex.ts:12-21 (canonical formula), lodgist/lib/actions/calculateTruthIndex.ts:33-204 (competing implementation), lodgist/app/api/listings/[id]/trust/route.ts:25 (calls initializeTrustComponents), packages/ai-core/src/utils/fraudChecks.js:1–145 (parallel fraud scoring), lodgist/__tests__/calculateTruthIndex.test.ts:94 (max score=60 with current schema gaps), packages/ai-core/__tests__/fraudChecks.unit.test.js:36-153 (fraud check tests pass)
rubric.gap: DUAL ENGINES: Two unrelated truth index computations exist with different weights, different inputs, and different persistence targets. The canonical component-based engine (computeTruthIndex) is well-designed but the older calculateTruthIndex action is still importable and tested. No single source of truth. The fraudChecks.js signals (duplicate phone, price anomaly, image reverse search) are not integrated into either truth index computation — they live in a separate AI Core package with no bridging code to the main Lodgist trust flow.
rubric.action_owner: Backend lead + CTO-architect — unify to single canonical engine, deprecate calculateTruthIndex action, wire fraudChecks signals as additional TrustComponents or pre-scoring filters

rubric.criterion: Fraud signal system — detection, reporting, resolution
rubric.a_plus: Three signal channels operational: (1) System auto-detection — duplicate phone check, price anomaly check, image reverse search wired into listing creation/update flow, results persisted as FraudSignal records with SIGNAL_SOURCE=SYSTEM; (2) User report flow — public 'Report this listing' CTA creates FraudSignal with SIGNAL_SOURCE=USER_REPORT; (3) Admin resolution workflow — admin can investigate, mark OPEN→INVESTIGATING→RESOLVED/DISMISSED with notes. Fraud signals visible to admin only, never exposed to public API. Signals feed into listing riskState transitions.
rubric.current_state: Schema has FraudSignal model (fraudSignalType, severity, source, status, resolvedById, resolvedAt) and AIFraudSignal model (score, reasoning, metadata). lodgist/app/api/fraud-reports/route.ts handles user reports but only sets isFlaggedForFraud=true on the listing — does NOT create a FraudSignal record. packages/ai-core/src/utils/fraudChecks.js has working detection functions (checkDuplicateLandlordPhone, checkPriceAnomaly, performImageReverseSearch) with comprehensive unit tests, but they are NOT wired into any Lodgist listing flow — they live in a separate package with no integration bridge. fraudDetectionService.ts (lodgist/lib/services/) is a stub using Math.random() — not production. No admin resolution UI or endpoint exists. No system auto-detection hook exists on listing create/update.

rubric.criterion: Listing risk state — state machine, transitions, visibility
rubric.a_plus: Listing.riskState is a controlled state machine with 5 states (VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED, UNDER_REVIEW, FLAGGED, SUSPENDED). Transitions are event-driven: submission→UNDER_REVIEW, approval→VERIFIED, rejection→UNVERIFIED, fraud confirmation→FLAGGED, admin suspension→SUSPENDED. Every transition is logged. Public API surfaces riskState on listings and trust endpoint. Frontend renders appropriate badge per state. No direct DB writes bypass the state machine.
rubric.current_state: Schema defines RiskState enum and listing.riskState field with default UNVERIFIED. The trust API route returns riskState. The admin stats endpoint counts flagged listings. However: no state transition logic exists in app code — riskState is only ever set by seed data and never changed by any endpoint. The fraud report endpoint sets isFlaggedForFraud=true but does NOT change riskState to FLAGGED. The verification submit endpoint (console.log stub) does not set UNDER_REVIEW. No state machine guards exist to prevent invalid transitions (e.g., VERIFIED→FLAGGED without review). Frontend PropertyCard derives its own verification state from truthIndex numbers (getVerificationState function) rather than using the actual riskState field — this creates a dual state representation.
rubric.evidence: prisma schema listing.riskState:181 (field exists, default UNVERIFIED), prisma schema RiskState enum:519-525 (5 states defined), lodgist/app/api/fraud-reports/route.ts:43-51 (sets isFlaggedForFraud, NOT riskState), lodgist/app/api/verify/route.ts (no riskState transition), lodgist/components/PropertyCard.tsx:73-79 (getVerificationState derives state from truthIndex, ignoring riskState field), lodgist/app/api/listings/[id]/trust/route.ts:18 (reads riskState but doesn't transition it), packages/db/prisma/seed-trust.ts:113-160 (seed sets riskState directly, no transition logic)
rubric.gap: NO STATE MACHINE. riskState is a passive database field with no transition logic. The fraud report flow sets a boolean flag but doesn't transition riskState. The verification submit flow doesn't transition riskState. Frontend derives its own state from truthIndex numbers (PropertyCard.getVerificationState) creating inconsistency between backend state and frontend display. No guards prevent invalid transitions. No audit trail for state changes (AdminAction not written for riskState changes).
rubric.action_owner: Backend lead — implement state transition functions with guards, wire into verification and fraud flows, log AdminAction on every transition. Frontend — use riskState from API, not derived from truthIndex.

Fraud detection functions (checkDuplicateLandlordPhone, checkPriceAnomaly, performImageReverseSearch) are fully implemented and unit-tested in packages/ai-core but are completely orphaned — no integration bridge to main Lodgist trust flow

Public verification endpoint (app/api/verify/route.ts) logs to console only — no DB persist, no file upload, no auth check, no VerificationRequest creation; the TODO comment explicitly acknowledges this
User fraud reports (app/api/fraud-reports/route.ts) set isFlaggedForFraud boolean on listing but never create a FraudSignal record — the FraudSignal table is bypassed entirely
fraudDetectionService.ts uses Math.random() > 0.5 as fraud determination — explicitly a demo stub, not production code
No admin override endpoints exist: no risk state override, no verification approve/reject, no fraud signal resolve, no trust component management — AdminAction table exists but is never written to

frontend PropertyCard derives verification state from truthIndex numbers (getVerificationState) rather than using the backend riskState field — dual state representation creates inconsistency
VerificationRequest, FraudSignal, and AdminAction tables exist in schema with correct relations and enums but have no write endpoints in the Next.js app router
CLAUDE.md Phase 2 status (IN PROGRESS) is inaccurate — no Phase 2 deliverables exist; should be NOT STARTED

GET /api/listings/[id]/trust calls initializeTrustComponents on every request — creates default components if missing, which is a side effect on a read endpoint and would reset any custom component state
No file upload provider detected in package.json (no cloudinary, @aws-sdk, @vercel/blob, uploadthing) — verification flow cannot implement document upload without adding a provider
No email provider detected in package.json (no resend, nodemailer, sendgrid) — verification status notifications cannot be sent
The backend Express verification routes (backend/src/routes/verification.js) are stubs returning mock JSON — /approve and /reject do not perform any DB operations
flagged_for_founder: Dual truth index engines create a correctness risk: which score is 'real' — the component-based one on the listing or the property-based one in TruthIndexScore? These can disagree and there is no reconciliation process. This is a data integrity issue that will compound as the platform grows.

The fraud detection package (packages/ai-core) has real, tested detection logic that is completely disconnected from the main app. This is sunk investment — the code exists, tests pass, but it protects nothing because it's not wired in. Founder decision: integrate now or deprecate.

The verification flow is the core trust promise ('Verified Property. Zero Fraud.') but the submit endpoint is a console.log stub. The Phase 3 doc is complete but unimplemented. This is the gap between marketing promise and product reality — highest priority trust surface.

Admin operations have zero UI for trust workflows. The admin can see stats but cannot approve verifications, resolve fraud signals, or override risk states. If a flagged listing needs urgent action, the only path is direct DB manipulation — unsafe for production.

No file storage or email provider is installed. The Phase 3 verification flow requires both. Adding these is a dependency decision (Cloudinary vs Vercel Blob vs S3 for files; Resend vs Nodemailer for email) that blocks the entire verification flow.

The /api/verify endpoint and the backend Express verification stubs suggest verification was started in two places independently. Clarify which is the canonical path before building — otherwise you'll have three parallel verification implementations.
